verdicts.reason: A jams the CTA and the three spec chips into a messy cluster in the top-left corner, ahead of the logo and headline. That breaks the reading order and buries the CTA. A also leaves an orphaned 'waited' on the headline and a large empty band above the tiny legal text. B keeps the order logo → headline → action, with the headline wrapped cleanly. But B's CTA sits in one row with the chips at the same weight, so it no longer stands out. The 142 G pill is oversized and set apart by an uneven gap, and the left-aligned logo is cramped against the headline.

A has a clear headline → shoe → action order. Its flaws: the logo is pushed down to the bottom-left next to the fine print, which weakens the brand. The CTA is lost in a row of same-size chips, the 142 G pill is uneven, and the legal text is right-aligned while everything else is centered. B is the broken layout from pair 1: the CTA and chips are crammed into the top-left corner, 'waited' is orphaned, and there is dead space at the bottom.

A is closest to the original: centered logo, then shoe, then a three-line headline that wraps well, then actions and legal text, with good margins. But the CTA shares one row with the spec chips at the same weight, so it doesn't stand out the way the original's centered button did. The 142 G pill is also oversized and unevenly spaced. B is the same broken layout: CTA and chips tangled in the top-left corner, the reading order jumbled, an orphaned 'waited', and an empty lower third.
